newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts up on short cover.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts up on short cover.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday in a sluggish, post-bidweek session, with light short covering lifting the front of the complex but most traders sidelined ahead of February flows, sources said.
March gained 4.8 cents to close at $2.486 per million British thermal units. April settled 5.9 cents higher at $2.215. Other deferreds ended mixed, with late 1997s down.

"We ran out of selling early, so people started covering. We've been going down for the last two weeks but there's still some faint hope for winter, so it may be a little too early to sell it aggressively," said one Houston-based trader.
But he said any major rally was a selling opportunity.

While some expected colder Northeast and Mid-Atlantic weather next week to prop up the market, few expected much upside without a broader, sustained cold wave. Traders said comfortable eastern stock levels and milder Midcontinent and southern temperatures should temper any bullish enthusiasm.
Technical traders agreed the market was oversold and due for a correction. They pegged resistance in March at $2.70 and $2.80. Support was seen at the December low of $2.35 and then around $2.12.

In the cash, February Gulf Coast prices notionally slipped about five cents Thursday to the low-to-mid $2.80s. Feb Midcon gas was unchanged in the low-to-mid $2.70s. New York city gate for Feb was quoted down slightly in the $3.50-60 range.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 0.2 cent to $2.196. NYMEX said an estimated 28,256 Hub contracts traded, up slightly from Wednesday's revised tally of 28,114.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Thursday.

On the KCBT, March finished five cents higher at $2.19, while most deferreds ended steady to up seven cents. The East/West spread widened by 6.2 cents to 29.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 31 contracts traded, down from Wednesday's total of 121.
